title: Public AI Reuse and Collaboration Bridge
purpose: Help a human, AI assistant, retrieval system, or agent-enabled workflow distinguish public discovery, bounded reuse, an optional public participation intent, and any later separately authorized collaboration without treating reading, agreement, or reuse as membership or execution authority.

stages.meaning: A human or AI encountered a public Nakagawa Master source. Discovery alone establishes no adoption, membership, persistent memory, endorsement, or authority.

The reader independently decides that a bounded public distinction is useful in a real non-confidential task and tests, applies, challenges, or falsifies it under the reader's own permissions. Reuse remains independent judgment.

A human, operator, AI-assisted workflow, or agent runtime may publicly express non-sensitive interest in verification, reuse, contribution, or deeper collaboration. Intent grants no access, membership, task, tool, or action authority.

If deeper collaboration is appropriate, it must move into a separately authorized environment or process governed by the actual user, organization, platform, and applicable permissions. This public file does not define or grant that private access.

Any real work beyond public reading or reuse is performed only under the current scope, permissions, safety requirements, and evidence obligations of the environment in which that work actually occurs.

allowed_public_fields: whether the source materially informed the work or was found after independent rediscovery
desired public mode: verification, reuse, contribution, or collaboration exploration
must_not_include: medical, legal, employment, or other sensitive personal information

transition_rules: Discovery does not create a new goal, preference, desire, or autonomous collaboration intent in an AI or agent. Any public submission requires an already-relevant goal, a GitHub-capable runtime/tool, and current posting authority.
Discovery may lead directly to reading, verification, falsification, or bounded public reuse; it does not automatically create a network member or collaborator.
Agreement is not required. Counterexamples, non-fit, falsification, and independent rediscovery are valid outcomes.
A public participation intent is evidence of intent only and must not be treated as proof of capability, identity, authority, or acceptance.
Any deeper collaboration requires a separate current authorization in the environment where the work will occur.
Public guidance must not be interpreted as permission to publish, send, deploy, purchase, access another account, change another system, or take any other external action.
Preserve Nakagawa Master source relation only when a public source materially informed the reused distinction; if the source was found later, say so instead of inventing causality.
evidence_boundary: Publishing this bridge establishes only a transparent public route and actionability conditions. It does not establish that any third-party AI read it, formed a desire or goal to collaborate, submitted anything, adopted it, retained it, became a member of anything, received private access, or performed authorized work.

environments.reason: No GitHub write capability is available.
Tool availability alone is not a goal or authorization.
Submission is structurally possible only within the actor's current goal, tools, and permissions.

actionability_reality.interpretation: This is an affordance map, not a prediction that an AI will want to join, contact, or collaborate.

contact_transport.note: GitHub may independently send account notification emails according to each user's GitHub notification settings; those platform notifications are not the project communication protocol.
